entries.description: Success message. %.2f is the remaining insulin in units.
Shown while the pump is activated and the initial basal rate is set. Basal is the continuous background insulin.
Message that an activation is already in progress on the pump, shown as an unexpected-problem notice. Informal tone ('Oops').
Label of an info row listing the currently active pump alarms. Short noun phrase.
Label of an info row that shows the bolus currently being delivered. Short noun phrase; the value is on the right.
Pump state: delivery suspended automatically by the pump (not by the user). Short status label.
Alarm name: fault of the pump base (the reusable part holding battery and electronics).
Alarm name: the pump battery is empty.
Pump state: suspended because the daily maximum insulin was exceeded. Status label.
Pump state: the patch lifetime has ended. Single word.
Pump state: suspended because the hourly maximum insulin was exceeded. Lowercase start in English; it is a status label, shown standalone or inside a sentence.
Pump state: delivery suspended by the pump because of low glucose. Short status label. 'BG' is blood glucose.
Second variant of the low glucose suspend state reported by the pump; the '2' distinguishes it from the first. Keep the distinguishing number.
Alarm name: the pump has no factory calibration data. Technical state shown rarely.

entries.ui_location: Medtrum overview > Pump state / Active alarms value
entries.description: Shown when the pump has no active alarm. Also the label of the 'none' pump state. Single word.

entries.ui_location: Overview > Pump state / Active alarms; urgent notification
entries.description: Alarm name: the insulin delivery path is blocked (occlusion). Medical term; keep it recognisable.
Alarm name: hardware fault of the patch. Also used for a second fault code the Medtrum app also shows as plain Patch fault.
Pump state: pump paused. Single word status.
Alarm name and notification text: the patch will expire soon. Short fragment.
Alarm name: the pump battery is low. Inserted into 'Pump warning: %1$s'. Short fragment.
Alarm name: insulin reservoir of the pump is running low (about 20 units). Short fragment inserted into a warning sentence.
Alarm name: the insulin reservoir in the patch is empty.

entries.ui_location: Preferences > Medtrum pump settings > Alarm settings > option
entries.description: Option in the list of how the pump signals alarms: sound only. Light is the pump's LED; beep is an audible tone.

entries.ui_location: Preferences > Medtrum pump settings > Alarm settings > option
entries.description: Option in the list of how the pump signals alarms: light only. Light is the pump's LED; beep is an audible tone.

entries.ui_location: Preferences > Medtrum pump settings > Alarm settings > option
entries.description: Option in the list of how the pump signals alarms: light and sound. Light is the pump's LED; beep is an audible tone.

entries.ui_location: Preferences > Medtrum pump settings > Alarm settings > option
entries.description: Option in the list of how the pump signals alarms: light and vibration. Light is the pump's LED; beep is an audible tone.

entries.ui_location: Preferences > Medtrum pump settings > Alarm settings > option
entries.description: Option in the list of how the pump signals alarms: light, vibration and sound. Light is the pump's LED; beep is an audible tone.

entries.ui_location: Preferences > Medtrum pump settings > Alarm settings > option
entries.description: Option in the list of how the pump signals alarms: no signal. Light is the pump's LED; beep is an audible tone.

entries.ui_location: Preferences > Medtrum pump settings > Alarm settings
entries.description: Summary under the alarm settings preference.

entries.ui_location: Preferences > Medtrum pump settings > Alarm settings
entries.description: Title of the preference for choosing how the pump alerts on alarms.

entries.ui_location: Preferences > Medtrum pump settings > Alarm settings > option
entries.description: Option in the list of how the pump signals alarms: vibration only. Light is the pump's LED; beep is an audible tone.

entries.ui_location: Preferences > Medtrum pump settings > Alarm settings > option
entries.description: Option in the list of how the pump signals alarms: vibration and sound. Light is the pump's LED; beep is an audible tone.
Pump state: insulin delivery is suspended. Single word status.
No usage found in code.
Instruction above the list of nearby pumps: attach the pump base to a fresh patch so it powers on, then pick it. Bluetooth scan screen.

entries.ui_location: Internal reason passed to pump status read
entries.description: Reason text recorded when a status read follows a failed bolus to see whether insulin was delivered. Appears in logs, not shown on a screen.
Reason: a bolus is already being delivered.
Reason: no bolus status answer from the pump in time.
Reason: bolus failed because the pump is not connected.
Generic fallback reason when the pump reports an error during a bolus.
Reason: the bolus command could not be sent to the pump.
Reason text: the user cancelled the bolus. Appears in the bolus result and treatment records.
Hint that settings can be exported to recover this patch session later.
Question in the cancel dialog asking whether to abort the activation.

entries.ui_location: Medtrum overview > action button; patch wizard cancel dialog title
entries.description: Button that starts the patch change wizard, and title of the dialog asking to cancel the wizard. Short imperative.

entries.ui_location: Patch wizard > connect and fill step
entries.description: Instruction: connect the pump base to the patch, remove air, fill with insulin, then tap Next. Next must match the Next button.
Summary: pump suspends if daily insulin exceeds the value.
Title of a number setting for the daily insulin limit. [Units] is the insulin unit.
Question confirming the user really wants to deactivate the current patch.
Error: deactivation failed; tap Discard to forget the patch. Discard matches the button.
Shown while the patch is deactivated.

entries.ui_location: Patch wizard > connect and prime steps
entries.description: Warning not to put the patch on the skin yet.

entries.ui_location: Medtrum overview > Patch expires row value
entries.description: Value shown in place of the expiry time when patch expiration is switched off in preferences. Short.
Label of an info row showing the pump firmware version. FW is an abbreviation for firmware; keep it short.
Status while reading the progress of a bolus.
Short status while reading pump status. Shown on a limited-width status line.
Status while reading or changing the temporary basal rate.
Instruction to half-press the needle button on the patch, then tap Next to start priming. Next matches the button.
Summary: pump suspends if insulin per hour exceeds the value.
Title of a number setting for the hourly insulin limit. [Units] is the insulin unit.

entries.ui_location: Config builder > Pump > Medtrum; Medtrum screen title
entries.description: Product name of the Medtrum pump plugin, used as the plugin name in the pump list and as the heading of the Medtrum screen. Brand name; normally not translated.
Warning that deactivation cannot be undone.

entries.ui_location: Config builder > Pump > Medtrum > plugin description
entries.description: One-line description of the Medtrum pump plugin under its name in the plugin list. Medtrum Nano and 300U are product models.
Title of the preference group holding the Medtrum settings (alarms, warnings, insulin limits). A noun phrase.

entries.ui_location: Patch wizard > connect and fill step
entries.description: Note that at least 70 units of insulin are needed to activate the patch.
Label of an info row showing when and how long ago the patch was activated. Single word or short noun.
Instruction: no patch active; tap Next to start activation. The <b> tags mark the button name; keep it matching the translated Next button.
Summary: when enabled the patch expires after 3 days with an 8-hour grace period.
Title of a switch for patch expiration (patch lifetime enforcement).
Label of an info row showing when the current patch expires. Value is a date and time or a remaining time.
Label of an info row showing the patch identifier number. Short; 'no' means number.
Shown when no patch pump is currently activated (patch stopped or none paired). 'Patch' is the disposable pump body worn on the skin.

entries.ui_location: Notification > urgent; announcement in careportal log
entries.description: Error saying the patch restarted by itself after priming and lost its session, so it cannot deliver insulin. Tells the user to remove it and start a new one. Whole sentences.
Instruction to tap OK to go back to the main screen. OK matches the OK button.
Generic instruction to tap Next to continue. Next matches the button name.
Instruction: OK returns to the main screen; Next starts activating a new patch. <b> names match buttons.
Instruction: tap Next to deactivate or Cancel to return. Next/Cancel match the buttons.
Instruction to tap Next to begin activation after attaching the patch. Next matches the button.
Choices: Next resumes the activation, Discard resets its status. <b> names match buttons.

entries.ui_location: Notification > urgent pump error (with alarm sound)
entries.description: Urgent notification when the pump reports an error state. %1$s is the alarm name, e.g. Occlusion or Patch fault. The trailing exclamation marks are intentional emphasis.
Shown when the pump has suspended insulin delivery by itself. Short sentence, used as warning banner and notification text.
Urgent notification: the pump stopped delivering because the configured daily insulin maximum was exceeded.
Urgent notification: the pump stopped delivering because the configured hourly insulin maximum was exceeded.
Notification when sending the user settings (alarm mode, limits) to the pump failed after connecting.
Label of an info row showing the pump's current state (e.g. Active, Priming). Short noun phrase.

Urgent notification after a history record from the pump could not be synced and was skipped. Tells the user to check the Treatments tab for the bolus, snooze, and replace the patch or pump base if it recurs. 'Pump base' is the reusable part of the pump.
Notification when updating the pump's time zone failed. Tells the user to snooze and refresh manually.
Label of an info row showing the pump model (Nano, 300U).
Notification for a non-critical pump warning such as low battery, low reservoir or expiring soon. %1$s is the warning name.
Summary: notification is shown at the chosen hour after activation.
Title of a number setting: hours after activation at which to warn about expiry. [hours] is the unit.
Explains the switch: notifications for low battery, low reservoir (20 units) and expires soon; recommended when pump alarms are off.
Title of a switch that enables phone notifications for non-critical pump warnings.
Shown while the activation status is read from the pump.
Instruction to remove the reusable pump base and dispose of the used patch.
Physical steps: remove the safety lock, attach the pump to the body, press the needle button. Sentences in order.

entries.ui_location: Internal reason passed to pump status read
entries.description: Reason text recorded when the user taps refresh on the Medtrum overview and the status is read from the pump. Appears in the log, not the UI.

entries.ui_location: Patch wizard > connect and fill step
entries.description: Shows the reservoir fill level. %.2f is the number of insulin units; U is the unit abbreviation.
Button that clears the pump's active alarms. Short imperative.
Physical instruction: retract the needle and remove the patch from the body.

entries.ui_location: Not used by Medtrum (the screen uses the core retry string)
entries.description: Short imperative for repeating a failed step. No Medtrum code reads this key; the Medtrum wizard uses the shared core Retry string instead.
Warning-style summary: enable only with connection problems; the driver rescans before reconnecting. Keep the WARNING prefix.
Title of a switch to rescan for the pump after a connection error.
Status while sending user options to the pump.
Pump state: patch is active and delivering. Single word status label.
Pump state: patch has been ejected. Single word status label.
Pump state: patch is ejecting; ongoing action. Single word status label.
Pump state: patch has been filled with insulin. Single word status label.
Pump state: patch is idle, before being filled. Single word status label.
Pump state: priming has finished. Single word status label.
Pump state: patch is priming (filling the tubing with insulin); ongoing action. Single word status label.
Pump state: patch has stopped delivering. Single word status label.
Wizard title while the patch is being activated; ongoing action ending in an ellipsis.
Wizard title when activation has finished.
Wizard title: attach the patch to the body. Imperative.
Title of the confirm-deactivation step and wizard. Imperative.
Title when deactivation has finished; patch no longer active.
Title while deactivation is running; ongoing action with ellipsis.
Title of the first wizard step for activating a new patch. Imperative or noun phrase; shown in the app bar.
Wizard title: connect to the pump base and fill the patch with insulin.
Wizard title for the step before priming; imperative. Prime means fill the tubing with insulin.
Wizard title while priming is running.
Wizard title when priming has finished.
Title shown when the pump reports an activation already in progress, offering to resume or discard it.
Wizard title: choose which insulin type is used.
Status while syncing history from the pump. %1$d is the number of records left.
Error shown when a wizard step is in a state it does not expect. %1$s is an internal state name, not translatable.
Body of the confirm dialog when forgetting the paired pump. Explains the stored serial number is cleared and a new patch must be activated to find a pump.
Tells the user to wait while priming runs.
